layers.text: A1 To thousandfold ever remembered, respected brother Wazurg-ummēd, *keeper of the archives (next line) in *Haspīn-raz, and Wīrgušnasp the Elder, reverence! A2 Xradzād (with) many greetings at least B Farroxgušnasp the scribe from the village of *Haspīn-raz in the “house” of Dēl-Dēlān on behalf of a statement to the residence of the King of Parišwārgar, protected by the gods (line 4), who (was) in *Halīg came before me (saying): B1 one Yazdfarrox by name from the village of *Haspīn-raz in that “house” (district), because of his wife, Yazdweh by name, the pādixšāy-daughter of Farroxgušnasp on behalf of the guardianship of Farroxgušnasp. Thus he kept her spring after spring and in his own matrimony so many years as one of his own and now without reason a defamation regarding Yazdweh arose that he would not settle both to give (her daily) sustenance and (additional) allocation and work-related income and clothing and some surplus to be given. And during that procedure he stated before me the baselessness (of the accusation). B2 You because of this matter you should summon (xwāhēd, line 14) Yazdfarrox, son of Farroxgušnasp Gušnasp-Frayād, (so that) he may know of the matter. And if the surplus income as declared by Farroxgušnasp becomes evident you should give the order to Yazdfarrox to satisfy Farroxgušnasp on that matter. If something else with regard to this matter becomes evident, in detail and clearly, in (your) answer to me you should show, (and) you should summon him (Yazdfarrox) directly from that place together with Farroxgušnasp to the service of the residence before me and make known (it) also to the palace service attendant. Bz The letter month Mihr (7th month) in the year 104 (PYE = 755/6 CE) day Frawardīn (19th day) ordered to make.

layers.text: A māh Amurdād abar sāl 106 ī pas az ōy bay Yazdgird šāhān šāh ī nab ī ōy bay Xusrō ī Ōhrmazdān ud rōz Wahman ka Wazurgummēd ēd kē tasūg ī *dar-espāsbed ī abar Dumbāwand ī dādestān čiyōnīh tasūg ham pondik wanīh ī abar Dumbāwand wisp tan must pad-iš friy būdan pad mānīhā sōzišn ham tasūg ī pondik wanīh būd B mardān ī Bōxt nām ō Wazurgummēd guft kū mardān ī Ērāngušnasp nām Kurd pus ham tasūg ī pondik wanīh az xwāstag sūd im rōz Wahman Ērāngušnasp xwāstag arz s(atēr) 5 sēm dōšīh ī mardān ī Šahrdēlān nām Yazdōy pus ān ōbastag deh mānēd az Šahrdēlān abāyēd pad kard ān xwāstag ahy wizārdan harw s(atēr) 5 gandum g(rīw) 5 waxš ō Šahrdēlān dādan tazāg pas hamē ka Šahrdēlān gandum xwāhēd pad pašt ī stēzag ō Šahrdēlān dādan agar tis-iz ǰuttar kunēm tāwān-iz arz s(atēr) 3 ō Šahrdēlān dād rāy Wahman-iz abāg Šahrdēlān paymān kard kū en guftag ham ō tōzišn rasēd ud paččēn ēw kunēh ō tō nē dēbahr ī man rāy ka pēšēn-tar n Ābān ud Wahrām ud Ērāngušnasp āgenēn kard ī tis rasēd ī man pad-iz muhr ī tō wizīr āwištan abāg tō harw pad kabīz ī tāwān wizīr bawēd ◯ ud Ērāngušnasp-iz ān Bōxt guft rāst ud Wazurgummēd ud kē nazd mānist ◯ ud Ērāngušnasp guft kū im māh Amurdād abar sāl 106 ud rōz Wahman man xwāstag arz s(atēr) 5 sēm dōšīh ī Šahrdēlān ān Bōxt guft az Šahrdēlān ī ham tasūg hamāg guft čiy[ō]n Bōxt guft paymān kard ud tis-iz ī abar Bōxt guft ōwōn did nibēsēd ud guft ān ◯ C ud ēn nāmag pad muhr ī paččēngarīh ī Mihrīg ī ham tasūg ī *dar-espāsbed čiyōnīh ī ham tasūg ī pondik wanīh pad must pad-iš framūd kištag framūd kištagān ud Wazurgummēd ud Raz deh ī-š dibīr muhr ī Farroxzād kē kard ud Ērāngušnasp āwišt ◯◯

layers.text: A month Amurdād (5th month) in the year 106 (757/8 CE) of late Lord Yazdgird, King of Kings, grandson of the late Lord Xusrō, son of Ōhrmazd, and day Wahman (2nd day) when Wazurgummēd who was (būd, line 5) responsible in the district of the chief of the service (of the residence) of Dumbāwand over the current (business) of the Law as well as the current (business) of everyone of the living beings (in the district of the) »Hazelnut Groves« of Dumbāwand to provide love instead of violence for the burning of the houses in the same district of the »Hazelnut Groves« B The people of Bōxt by name to Wazurgummēd said that the people of Ērāngušnasp by name, son of Kurd, also from the district of beyond the vineyards from the profit of the possessions this day Wahman Ērāngušnasp a sum worth 5 staters in silver as support for the people of Šahrdēlān by name, son of Yazdōy, who lives in the fallen village. From Šahrdēlān it is necessary to pay the money for the affair at the soonest all 5 staters in addition 5 grīw of wheat to be given to Šahrdēlān (and) afterwards persistently whenever Šahrdēlān asks for wheat according to the actual agreement of the quarrel (wheat) is to be given to Šahrdēlān. If I act but a little bit otherwise an additional compensation of 3 staters worth to be given to Šahrdēlān, Wahman together with Šahrdēlān is to make an agreement that this which has been spoken exactly arrives at (its) rectification and a copy is to be acquired so that you should not become angry when it will be not earlier than day Ābān (10th day) and day Wahrām (20th day) and together with Ērāngušnasp it was determined when the matter is due with your seal, there is a decision with you on everything of the quotaNote of the recompense. And Ērāngušnasp and that Bōxt said “right” and Wazurgummēd and those who stayed (line 18) nearby. And Ērāngušnasp declared this month Amurdād in the year 106 and day Wahman I affirmed (line 20) money worth of 5 staters in silver as support of Šahrdēlān that Bōxt from Šahrdēlān of the same district on the whole as Bōxt has spoken he made an agreement even that little on which is to be spoken by Bōxt then he should write and he said so (confirmed it). ◯ C And this document with the seal of the *copy office of Mihrīg with the responsibility of the same district of the chief of the service (of the residence) and also of the same district of the »Hazelnut Grove(s)«. Therefore he demanded seeds and even more seeds forcefully and Wazurgummēd and the scribe of the Raz (wine) village (woth) the seal of Farroxzād who made (it) and Ērāngušnasp sealed (it).

               <ns0:lb n="14-15" xml:id="trans-p1-l14-15" />and a copy is to be acquired so that you should not become angry when it will be not earlier than day Ābān (10th day) and day Wahrām (20th day) and together with Ērāngušnasp it was determined when the matter is due with your
               <ns0:lb n="16" xml:id="trans-p1-l16" />seal, there is a decision with you on everything of the quotaNote of the recompense.
               <ns0:lb n="17" xml:id="trans-p1-l17" />And Ērāngušnasp and that Bōxt said “right” and Wazurgummēd and those who stayed (line 18) nearby.
               <ns0:lb n="18" xml:id="trans-p1-l18" />And Ērāngušnasp declared this month Amurdād in the year
               <ns0:lb n="19" xml:id="trans-p1-l19" />106 and day Wahman I affirmed (line 20) money worth of 5 staters in silver as support of
               <ns0:lb n="20" xml:id="trans-p1-l20" />Šahrdēlān that Bōxt from Šahrdēlān of the same district on the whole as
               <ns0:lb n="21" xml:id="trans-p1-l21" />Bōxt has spoken he made an agreement even that little on which is to be spoken by Bōxt
               <ns0:lb n="22" xml:id="trans-p1-l22" />then he should write and he said so (confirmed it). ◯ C And this document with the seal of the *copy office
               <ns0:lb n="23" xml:id="trans-p1-l23" />of Mihrīg with the responsibility of the same district of the chief of the service (of the residence) and also of the same district of
               <ns0:lb n="24" xml:id="trans-p1-l24" />the »Hazelnut Grove(s)«. Therefore he demanded seeds and even more seeds forcefully
               <ns0:lb n="25" xml:id="trans-p1-l25" />and Wazurgummēd and the scribe of the Raz (wine) village (woth) the seal of Farroxzād
               <ns0:lb n="26" xml:id="trans-p1-l26" />who made (it) and Ērāngušnasp sealed (it). 
            </ns0:ab>
         </ns0:div>

layers.text: A māh Day abar sāl 103 ī pas az ōy bay Yazdgird šāhān šāh ī nah ī ōy bay Xusrō ī Ōhrmazdān ud rōz Rašn ka Wanandpanāh kē tasūg ī Dēl ī Dēlān ī abar Taburestān dādestān čiyōnīh tasūg ī Sūrīgān ī abar Taburestān dādestān pad dehīhā(!) pad-iš framān sāxtan pad dehīhā pūdag ham tasūg ī Dēl ī Dēlān būd B mardān ī Bōxt nām ō Wanandpanāh guft kū mardān ī Frawardīn nām būd mardān ī Ātaxšbōyag nām būd kardērīh pus wispān ham tasūg ī Dēl ī Dēlān az ān Haspīn-raz deh būd hēnd ud mardān ī Yazdfarrox nām Dēlānfarrox pus mardān ī Windādyazd nām mardān ī Windādōhrmazd nām Zādānfarrox pus mardān ī Farrox-Xusrōyān nām Farrox-Xusrō pus az ān Haspīn-raz deh Farrox-Xusrōyān ōy Frawardīn duxt Rašnweh ud Windādyazd ud Windādōhrmazd ud Yazdfarrox ōy Ātaxšbōyag pusarāwandān ud xwāstagdārān B1 ud pad bun ī ān Haspīn-raz deh kišwzār zamīg ī kōfag xār-wanīgān xwānēnd g(rīw) I āhang kē az ēw zayt ī zamīg ī xwāstagdārān ​​​ī mardān ī Yazdgird nām būd ud any mard ud az ēw zayt ī zamīg ī xwāstagdārān ​​ī mardān ī Zādānfarrox nām būd ud az ēw zayt ī zamīg ī [xwāstag-paymāyagān-ī] Māhōy nām būd ud az ēw zayt ī zamīg ī xwāstagdārān ī mardān ī Māhanōš(?) nām būd sāmān | B2 ud zamīg ī [kōfag] ǰadārīh xwānēnd g(rīw) 2 āhang kē az ēw zayt ī zand ud az ēw zayt ī zamīg ī xwāstagdārān ī Dērā nām būd ud az ēw zayt ī zamīg ī xwāstagdārān ī mardān ī Farroxzād nām būd ud az ēw zayt Ï zamīg ī xwāstagdārān ī ōy Māh-ōš ud any mard sāmān | B3 ud zamīg ī kōfag wanīgarīh xwand g(rīw) I āhang kē az ēw zayt ī zamīg ī mardān ī Farroxān nām ud az ēw zayt ī zamīg ī mardān ī Farroxgušnasp nām ud az ēw zayt ī zamīg ī xwāstagdārān ī ōy Dērā ud az ēw zayt ī zamīg ī ham Farrox-Xusrōyān sāmān | B4 zamīg ī ī kōfag g(rīw) I k(abīz) 8 āhang kē az ēw zayt ī zamīg ud xānag ī xwastagdārān ī mardān ī Yazdōy nām būd ud any mard ud az ēw zayt ī zamīg ud xānag ī xwāstagdārān ī mardān ī ōy Dēra ud any mard ud az dō zayt ī čand ud rawišn ī zamānag drahm ī az ān Haspīn-raz deh sāmān | B5 ud xānag ud spinǰānagīh ud tis enyā abar nimāyēd ud wizandag kard rāy zyān ēwēn sē ǰādag az 6 bārag-bār ud ham tasūg ī Dēl ī Dēlān pad bun ī Frōd deh razists zamīg ī kōfag g(rīw) l k(abīz) 5 āhang kē az ēw zayt ī razist zamīg ī xwāstagdārān ī mardān ī Wahištān nām būd ud az ēw zayt ī zamīg ī xwāstagdārān ī mardān ī ōy Ātaxšbōyag ud az ēw zayt ī zamīg ī xwāstagdārān ī az ān Frōd deh ud az ēw zayt ī pēš sāmān | B6 ud raz ud sarw ud tis enyā abar nimāyēd ud ēd kard rāy zyān ēwēn sē ǰadag az sē bār dō bār ud kišwānzār zamīg ī kōfag ī ān-iz pad bun ī ān Haspīn-raz deh ud mayg-rist xwānēnd g(rīw) 3 āhang kē az zayt ī rēš ud az ēw zayt ī zamīg ī mardān ī Wahmandān nām xwāstagdārān ī mardān ī Wahmanpanāh nām būd ud az dō zayt ī zamīg ī Anagrān sāmān | B7 ud zamīg ī kōfag asp-tāzān xwānēnd g(rīw) āhang kē az ēw zayt ī rēš ud az ēw zayt ī zamīg ī xwāstagdārān ī mardān ī Ērāzād nām būd ud az ēw zayt ī zamīg ī mardān ī Āzādxusrō nām {ud az ēw zayt ī zamīg ī mardān ī Āzādxusrō nām sāmān} | B8 ud zamīg ī [kōfag] damēnag ul-(ā)mad ī kišw ī g(rīw) l āhang kē az ēw zayt ī škihist ud az ēw zayt ī zamīg ī xwāstagdārān ī ōy Dēlānfarrox ud az ēw zayt ī zamīg ī Anagrān ud az ēw zayt ī zamīg ī mardān ī Dābōy nām ud any mard sāmān | B9 ud zamīg ī kōfag hurām xwānēnd zayt g(rīw) 6 āhang kē az dō zayt ī zamīg ī mardān ī Dābōy nām ud any mard uz az ēw zayt ī zamīg ī mardān ī Wangird nām ud az ēw zayt ī zamīg ī mardān ī Frawardīndād nām sāmān | Bfinal ud xānag ud spinǰānagīh ud kunǰid ud sarw ud tis enyā abar nimāyēd ud gannāg kard rāy zyān ēwēn ōy Frawardīn xwēš ǰadag ud tan ī Frawardīn ēwēn pad ān Frawardīn saxt kard rāy Frawardīn pad paymān ī Frawardīn kard dastwarīh ō xwēšīh ud dārišn ī Farrox-Xusrōyān madan Yazdfarrox ud Windādōhrmazd ud Windādyazd ōy xwāstag nē būd čē abāg Farrox-Xusrōyān guftan abar pahikārdan nē tis rāst ud ka ēd xīr ōwōn čiyōn man guft būd ēstād Windādōhrmazd ud Windādyazd ud Yazdfarrox ōy xwāstag kē tō sāmān pad nāmagīhā ud ō xwēšīh ud dārišn ī Farrox-Xusrōyān madan guft nē az im rōz Rašn frāz pad tis-iz ēwēnag abar ud abāg Farrox-Xusrōyān ud Windādōhrmazd ud Windādyazd ud Yazdfarrox āgenēn ōwōn čiyōn nē pahikārdan harw kē pad dastwarīh ī Windādōhrmadzd ud Windādyazd ud Yazdfarrox āgenēn ud tasūg-iz ǰud pahikafēd az Farrox-Xusrōyān abēzār ud Farrox-Xusrōyān pad ān xīr arz 101 abāyistan ud agar tis-iz ǰuttar kunēd arz 202 drahm ō Farrox-Xusrōyān dād ud grawagān kē abāg Farrox-Xusrōyān paymān kard kū amā rāst handāxt rāst frēzān ī tō kāstan tis pad ān ēwēnag čē rāy pahikārd paymān kardan nē kōxšīd ud rāst wizārišnīh ī amā ān čē az paymān kard nē āmad nē ēwar nē paččēn ham ud Windādōhrmad ud Windādyazd ud Yazdfarrox āgenēn ud ēd az ham az ērmānīh ī man pad-iz muhr ī tō wizīr āwišt ud pēš tō azi-šān pad dīd čiyōn zaytēn wizīr ī l nīd ○ ud ān-iz Windādōhrmazd ud Windādyazd ud Yazdfarrox ī Bōxt guft pēš Wanandpanāh būd ud padistād ○ ud Windādōhrmazd ud Windādyazd ud Yazdfarrox guft kū im rōz Rašn amā ōwōn čiyōn Bōwt guft paymān kard ud ǰadišnīg-iz ān čē Bōxt guft ōwōn čiyōn Bōxt pattūg ast ○ ud abar ēn nāmag didom sāxt ēstād čihrān ī ayārīh ī tō ud nibišt ○ ud ēn nāmag pad muhr ī ham tasūg ī Dēl ī Dēlān čiyōnīh ham tasūg ī Sūrīgān pad dehīhā pad-iš framān sāxtan deh pad kārframān zāyistan ud Wanandpanāh ud Dērzamān ī dibīr ud muhr ī dehbedān kē kard ud az mardān ī Dād-Burz-Mihr nām Mihrpanāh pus mardān ī Yazdfarrox nām Yazdpanāh pus az ān Haspīn-raz deh ud abar ēwāzīh guft ud Windādōhrmazd ud Windādyazd [ud Wanandpanāh] ud Yazdfarrox āwišt ○○

layers.text: A Month Day (10th month) in the year 103 after the late Lord Yazdgird, King of Kings, grandson of the late Lord Xusrō, son of Ōhrmazd, and day Rašn (18th day), when Wanandpanāh who presided over the Law in the district of Dēl ī Dēlān in Taburestān and likewise in the “Syrian quarter” in Taburestān in the villages (and) therefore was in charge to prepare orders relating to rotten (crops) in the villages of Dēl ī Dēlān. B The people of Bōxt by name to Wanandpanāh spoke this: >>The people who belong to Frawardīn by name (and) the people who belong to Ātaxšbōyag by name, all (of them of) authoritative progeny, (of) the same tasūg of Dēl ī Dēlān from the village of *Haspīn-raz were present and the people of Yazdfarrox by name, son of Dēlānfarrox, the people of Windādyazd by name, the people of Windādōhrmazd by name, son of Zādānfarrox, the people of Farrox-Xusrōyān by name, son of Farrox-Xusrōy, from the village of *Haspīn-raz, the sons of Farrox-Xusrōy, Rašnweh, daughter of the late Frawardīn and Windādyazd and Windādōhrmazd and Yazdfarrox, the sons and heirs of the late Ātaxšbōyag B1 And disposal (line 7) of a field land on a slope in charge of the bun of the *Haspīn-raz village—“Thorn Groves” they call it—crops of 1 grīw which (are) from one olive tree of the land which belonged to the heirs of the people of Yazdgird by name and another man and from one olive tree of the land which belonged to the heirs of the people of Zādānfarrox by name and from one olive tree of the land which belonged to [the valuers of the property] of Māhōy by name and from one olive tree of the land which belonged to the heirs of the people of the late Māhanōš(?) by name and another man. B2 And disposal (line 9) of land [on a slope]—they call (it) “Maintenance”— with crops of 2 which (are) from one olive tree of the community and from one olive tree which belongs to the lands of the heirs of Dērā by name and from one olive tree of the land which belongs to the heirs of the people of Farroxzād by name, and from one olive tree of the land of the heirs of the late Māh-ōš and another man. B3 And disposal (line 10) of crops of 1 grīw from land on a slope they call (it) “Waste” which come from one olive tree of the land of the people of Farroxān by name and from one olive tree of the land of the people of Farroxgušnasp by name and from one olive tree of the land of the heirs of the late Dērā and from one olive-tree of the land of the above Farrox-Xusrōyān. B4 Disposal of crops from land on a slope of 1 grīw 8 kabīz which (comes) from one olive tree of land and house which belong to the heirs of the people of Yazdōy by name and another man and from one olive tree of land and house which belong to the heirs of the late Dērā and another man, and from two olive trees according to the current value from the village of *Haspīn-raz. B5 And the costs of house and hospitality facilities and other matters you shall take in consideration and because of the damage due to the earthquake only one third from 6 mount loads. And (in) the same quarter of Dēl ī Dēlān (which is) in charge of the bun of the “Lower Village”, forested land on a slope with olives 1 grīw 5 kabīz: these (were) from one olive tree of forested land which belong to the heirs of the people of Wahištān by name, and from one olive-tree of the land of the heirs of the late Ātaxšbōyag, and from one olive tree of the land of their heirs which (is) from the “Lower village”, and from one olive tree which (is) before (the latter one). B6 And disposal of vines and cypresses and other things you shall take into consideration and because of this event a loss of one third of the norm instead of 3 loads only 2 loads and a field, an acre on a slope which also belongs to the bun of the community of *Haspīn-raz—they call it “Dead as a Locust”—a crop of 3 grīw which (comes) from a damaged olive tree and from (an) olive tree of the land which belongs to the people of Wahmandād, heir of the men of Wahmanpanāh by name, and from 2 olive trees of the land of Anagrān. B7 And disposal of land of a slope—“Horse Paddock” they call it—the crop of 4 grīw: these (are) the following: from one damaged olive tree and from one olive tree of the land which belongs to the heirs of the people of Ērāzād by name and from one olive tree of the land of the people of Āzādxusrō by name {and from one olive tree of the people of Āzādxusrō by name}. B8 And disposal of land [of a slope] in a fan (with wind) coming up tillage of 1 grīw: these are the following: from one broken olive tree and from one olive tree of the people of Dābōy by name and another man. B9 And disposal (line 20) of a land of a slope—“the Blissful one” they call it—with a crop of olives: 5 grīw: these (are) the following: from two olive trees of the land of the people of Dābōy and another man, and from one olive tree of the people of *Wangird and from one olive tree of the land of the people of Frawardīndād by name. B10 The house and the hospitality (facilities) and the sesame and the cypresses and something else are involved and because of the damage (by that) evil event the late Frawardīn’s own share and body of Frawardīn for that Frawardīn because of that severe event Frawardīn made an agreement that the right (of disposal) should pass to the property and maintenance of Farrox-Xusrōyān (but) should not be in the right (of disposal) of Windādōhrmazd and Windādyazd and Yazdfarrox, for it (is) by no means proper to proceed against Farrox-Xusrōyān (and) to submit it. And if this matter (is) such as I have explained that property (line 23) of Windādōhrmazd and Windādyazd and Yazdfarrox of which you said that the disposal (is) in the books and should suffice for the property and maintenance of Farrox-Xusrōyān, not from this day Rašn onwards also about (other) things about. And Against Farrox-Xusrōyān and Windādōhrmazd and Windādyazd and Yazdfarrox jointedly there will be no litigating. Every person who claims (pahikafēd, line 25) the auctorship of Windādōhrmazd and Windādyazd and Yazdfarrox jointly and also in another district (is) without means against Farrox-Xusrōyān and he owes 101 drahms to Farrox-Xusrōyān for this matter and if he acts somehow otherwise he (is obliged) to give (dād, line 26) 202 drahms to Farrox-Xusrōyān. And (regarding) the mortgage of the usufruct for which they made an agreement with Farrox-Xusrōyān, thus: we allotted it equally. We did not strive to make a contract to diminish your equal dues by that manner of litigating. And our equal payment is that which did not come from the agreement made (is) neither assured nor a copy. Also Windādōhrmazd and Windādyazd and Yazdfarrox jointly and together with my humbleness even with your seal they sealed the document and in Your presence from them under inspection they married out one “olive decision”. — And exactly that which Bōxt said Windādōhrmazd and Windādyazd and Yazdfarrox before Wanandpanāh confirmed and promised. — And Windādōhrmazd and Windādyazd and Yazdfarrox said: this day Rašn we, as Bōxt has spoken, made the contract and also on imponderabilities which Bōxt mentioned. are, as Bōxt (said), permanent – And from this letter he established a second (one), in the same form with Your assistance, and wrote (it down), — Bz And he sealed (line 33) this letter with the seal of the same district of Dēl ī Dēlān likewise of the Syrian quarter to prepare an order concerning the villages (and) to investigate (them) by the overseer and Wanandpanāh and Dērzamān the scribe and by the seals of the landlords who made (the contract) and from the people of Dād-Burz-Mihr by name, son of Mihrpanāh, the people of Yazdānfarrox by name, son of Yazdpanāh from the village of *Haspīn-raz and declared (consent) unanimously, and Windādōhrmazd and Windādyazd [and Wanandpanāh] and Yazdfarrox sealed it.

layers.text: A1 To the lordly Ōstāndār, born with inherited knowledge, reverence! A2 (From) Ōhrmazd-pad-moγ A3 many greetings. B And since You, Sir, with regard to the *protection of the wine‐grower(s) because, this year 29 (PYE = 680–681 CE), by my asking regarding wine‐growing of the Kōm district, You ordered to commission a man (who) with You, Sir, a contract made (saying) that any time when for *protection a duty (will be due) on (our) separated religion—so as (is) the legal advisor’s speech to You, Sir, —You gave me order to do (this), if, because (rāy, line 8) of preparation and *duration of that pecuniary affair, You must bring it (i.e. drahm pad dēn), (then) I personally will take (it) and will pay. Bz And this letter, by the witnesses’ seals of Xwadāgird, I sealed. C1 To [the lordly Ōstāndār, born with inherited knowledge, reverence! C2 Ōhrmazd-pad-moγ].

               <ns0:lb n="4" xml:id="trans-p1-l4" />Der Tagesration für (im Werte von) 2 Satēr aus dem Vermögen (Zahl)
               <ns0:lb n="5" xml:id="trans-p1-l5" />der Mutter des Farroxzād
               <ns0:lb n="6" xml:id="trans-p1-l6" />wegen Stroh 2 Maß(?)
               <ns0:lb n="7" xml:id="trans-p1-l7" />den Dienern jemand (schon) vorher
               <ns0:lb n="8" xml:id="trans-p1-l8" />gegeben. Zādānfarrox (hat’s) gesiegelt.
            </ns0:ab>
         </ns0:div>

layers.text: A1 To thousand-fold remembered very honoured brother Xradzād, reverence! A2 Windād-Xw aršēd, the Parišwārgar rad, well-being and all happiness for You Sir, shall be! B1 Burzēn-Pērōz, the scribe, son of Farroxgušnasp from the village of *Haspīn-raz in the district of Dēl-Dēlān personally together with the *painter of adornments* came before me because of a complaint (saying:) B1 (that) Burzēn-Pērōz would request to being granted a period of grace for that business and (also) satisfaction that (is) legally binding regarding the following (case): one Dādgušnasp by name, son of *Ātars, together with one Yazd by name, brother, and one Rāstdād, son of Wištāsp, ane one Yazdsar, son of Dēlāzād, from the village of *Haspīn-raz by (an act of) violence and shouting one wife, Dēzā by name, the pādixšāy-wife of Burzēn-Pērōz, from her personal belongings jewellery and goblet(s) and how they would open the bag worth a total of 500 staters and carry away the stolen things, (therefore it is necessary) to ask in every place and to check the registers of every single person, —unless on that matter he ordered (it already)—to summon every single man and for satisfaction of Burzēn-Pērōz to make a decision and judgement from me to You, Sir, this (is the purpose of this) letter as otherwise it will not be possible that Burzēn-Pērōz would come to contentment and complaint still remains and regarding that matter having been ordered, (give) me an answer. If this matter is such as Burzēn-Pērōz complains for him and the (other) men to send further is not suitable. B2 Sir, if Burzēn-Pērōz is still complaining in form because of this property Dādgušnasp and those (other) men and his statement has been heard if it becomes evident (line 22), in this way as Burzēn-Pērōz stated that this property belongs to Dādgušnasp and those men, when (the day of Wahrām has passed, should reach at a decision and should give a judgement this for Burzēn-Pērōz because of the groundlessness and by way of a process Will result in satisfaction. If there is proof therein that is also written that order that it be registered in an additional manner Concerning the proof of this case write this explicitly and clearly in your answer, also Dādgušnasp you should order to name the men and to take a legal action against those who (are involved) in that manner with Burzēn-Pērōz to restore (it/them) to the man (preceding line). Bz The letter month Wahman (11th month) in the year 104 and day Wahrām (20th day) he ordered to make.— C1 To thousand-fold remembered very honoured brother Xradzād, reverence! C2 Windād-Xw aršēd, the Parišwārgar rad.

<ns0:div xmlns:ns0="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" type="translation" xml:lang="de">
            <ns0:ab xml:id="MP1025_trans-p1">
               <ns0:lb n="1" xml:id="trans-p1-l1" />A1 To thousand-fold remembered very honoured brother Xradzād, reverence!
               <ns0:lb n="2" xml:id="trans-p1-l2" />A2 Windād-Xw aršēd, the Parišwārgar rad, well-being and all happiness for You
               <ns0:lb n="3" xml:id="trans-p1-l3" />Sir, shall be! B1 Burzēn-Pērōz, the scribe, son of Farroxgušnasp
               <ns0:lb n="4" xml:id="trans-p1-l4" />from the village of *Haspīn-raz in the district of Dēl-Dēlān personally
               <ns0:lb n="5" xml:id="trans-p1-l5" />together with the *painter of adornments* came before me because of a complaint (saying:) B1 (that) Burzēn-Pērōz
               <ns0:lb n="6" xml:id="trans-p1-l6" />would request to being granted a period of grace for that business and (also) satisfaction that (is) legally binding
               <ns0:lb n="7" xml:id="trans-p1-l7" />regarding the following (case): one Dādgušnasp by name, son of *Ātars, together with one Yazd by name,
               <ns0:lb n="8" xml:id="trans-p1-l8" />brother, and one Rāstdād, son of Wištāsp, ane one Yazdsar, son of Dēlāzād,
               <ns0:lb n="9" xml:id="trans-p1-l9" />from the village of *Haspīn-raz by (an act of) violence and shouting one wife, Dēzā
               <ns0:lb n="10" xml:id="trans-p1-l10" />by name, the pādixšāy-wife of Burzēn-Pērōz, from her personal belongings jewellery and goblet(s)
               <ns0:lb n="11-12" xml:id="trans-p1-l11-12" />and how they would open the bag worth a total of 500 staters and carry away the stolen things, (therefore it is necessary) to ask in every place and to check the registers of every single person,
               <ns0:lb n="13-14" xml:id="trans-p1-l13-14" />—unless on that matter he ordered (it already)—to summon every single man and for satisfaction of Burzēn-Pērōz to make a decision and judgement from me to You, Sir,
               <ns0:lb n="15-16" xml:id="trans-p1-l15-16" />this (is the purpose of this) letter as otherwise it will not be possible that Burzēn-Pērōz would come to contentment and complaint still remains and regarding that matter having been ordered, (give) me an answer.
               <ns0:lb n="17" xml:id="trans-p1-l17" />If this matter is such as Burzēn-Pērōz complains for him
               <ns0:lb n="18" xml:id="trans-p1-l18" />and the (other) men to send further is not suitable. B2 Sir,
               <ns0:lb n="19" xml:id="trans-p1-l19" />if Burzēn-Pērōz is still complaining in form because of this property Dādgušnasp
               <ns0:lb n="20" xml:id="trans-p1-l20" />and those (other) men and his statement has been heard
               <ns0:lb n="21" xml:id="trans-p1-l21" />if it becomes evident (line 22), in this way as
               <ns0:lb n="22" xml:id="trans-p1-l22" />Burzēn-Pērōz stated that this property belongs to Dādgušnasp
               <ns0:lb n="23" xml:id="trans-p1-l23" />and those men, when (the day of Wahrām has passed, should reach at a decision and should give a judgement
               <ns0:lb n="24" xml:id="trans-p1-l24" />this for Burzēn-Pērōz because of the groundlessness and by way of a process
               <ns0:lb n="25" xml:id="trans-p1-l25" />Will result in satisfaction. If there is proof therein that is also written that order that it be registered in an additional manner
               <ns0:lb n="26" xml:id="trans-p1-l26" />Concerning the proof of this case write this explicitly and clearly in your answer, also Dādgušnasp
               <ns0:lb n="27" xml:id="trans-p1-l27" />you should order to name the men and to take a legal action against those who (are involved) in that manner with Burzēn-Pērōz
               <ns0:lb n="28" xml:id="trans-p1-l28" />to restore (it/them) to the man (preceding line). Bz The letter month Wahman (11th month) in the year 104 and day Wahrām (20th day)
               <ns0:lb n="29" xml:id="trans-p1-l29" />he ordered to make.—
               <ns0:lb n="30" xml:id="trans-p1-l30" />C1 To thousand-fold remembered very honoured brother Xradzād, reverence!
               <ns0:lb n="31" xml:id="trans-p1-l32" />C2 Windād-Xw aršēd, the Parišwārgar rad. 
            </ns0:ab>
         </ns0:div>

layers.text: on trust of the always very fortunate Ōstāndār truly (?) Windādburzmihr-ābād manager [this] month Šahrewar of the year 48 when the Ōstāndār, standing under the protection of the gods, from the "House" to the Estate (for) which 6 kabīz of garmak, (for the) Ōstāndār 1 grīw 4 kabīz and over this then (only) one receipt he sealed and apart (from) this profit for the transction it was not necessary to demand (another one) and this receipt Mihrpanāh with the witnesses' seals of Zādanfarrox (sealed).

layers.text: (To the) *keeper of the archives and the Elder in the village of *Asp-gurd Day Ardwahišt (3rd day). ◯ Burzēn-Pērōz, pādixšāy, from this village of *Asp-gurd came before me: the wife, Sazā by name, pādixšāy, the people of Xwāst-Dēlān and who live (mānēd, line 5) in the village of *Asp-gurd (and) the daughter who is also from there. The statement and entitlement and judement and agreement which made and sealed Xwāst-Dēlān for Burzēn-Pērōz came to be revealed to entering in marriage with Burzēn-Pērōz and Sazā (who has) the entitlement by this judgement as long as she is in matrimony with Burzēn-Pērōz [M] Dādgušnasp the scribe from the village of *Asp-gurd because of Sazā investigating on the marriage to Burzēn-Pērōz how it was to be cared for and with regard to the goblets and much wealth in a bag and jewellery being together with it by chance how everything (hā̆mist, line 11) was to be tied up. And Burzēn-Pērōz on this matter before the Rad sifted (the evidence) to that extent to be complained in a letter on these things and also to write so by Dādgušnasp on the groundlessness and injustice for the loss of Burzēn-Pērōz to be investigated and the document with assured (line 15) seal to be kept (line 15) together there is growing complaint on this matter to say: You (are) obstinate (lit. “rock”) when Burzēn-Pērōz (still) complains in this way and because of [this] matter he would inquire about bribery of the farmers and (their) wives and also Sazā. And from that statement he will hear of the reason of the matter he should know, moreover how the final (line 19) reason and statement by Sazā what exactly as answer of (rightness ?) he should write down and also Sazā and how much walth in the bag which Burzēn-Pērōz will confirm is particular and I am coming before you (for explaining) the reason why he was cheated even of the agreement: month Frawardīn of the year 106, day Ardwahišt (3rd day). From Dādborzmihr

layers.text: To Burz-Ādur, remembered by (the) god(s) ... (of) marriage according to the Mazdean rite: reverence! Received by Wehbūd and the other people in town well-being and health and all fortune over you (pl.) (may) be and ... in health and peace... like your (sg.) right word on your (pl.) behalf every bad [be dispersed] it is necessary, on this ..., too, ... it should be becasue people in town are in health. My letter and fit for you (sg.) he(?) brought from (the) town ... For I learnt from Burzag that you sealed the bundle and he wants to come because of the young husband-ship. They would come if it is fitting for you (pl.) of month Ādur and they would watch and from the letter which had been opened (other) people(?) would make a fire, for you (sg.) it was made well. When I by ... ... sent a message that you (pl.) hither should come ... ... gift ... to the mother was sent ... ... letter(?) ... in the hand there is not and the road(?) you(sg.)(?) [...] and on your (sg.) behalf something he should send [...] he will send, because of your (pl.) health I write the letter ... ... ... ... letter ... month Ādur ... …

               <ns0:lb n="3" xml:id="trans-p1-l3" />the young, all except 
               <ns0:lb n="4" xml:id="trans-p1-l4" />those who belong to the *household 
               <ns0:lb n="5-9" xml:id="trans-p1-l5-9" />of Namēwar, to organize a running, the quota (paymānag) again is 2 and a half man of *cottage cheese*, 500 nuts, 10 dōlag of wine to the maidservant 
               <ns0:lb n="10" xml:id="trans-p1-l10" />of the mother of 
               <ns0:lb n="11" xml:id="trans-p1-l11" />Yazdānpanāh 
               <ns0:lb n="12-14" xml:id="trans-p1-l12-14" />to be given personally. The Ōstāndār sealed the čak.
            </ns0:ab>
         </ns0:div>

layers.text: Lieblicher Geist Frēdōn an Ōhrmazd, den Herrn: du hast etwas anderes (falsches, gegensätzliches) als wunderbarer gesehen als dieses, was ich so wunderbar gesehen habe: daß die „Schlange“(?) den Kern versiegeln194 soll: dieses, was du gesehen hast, (ist) nicht wunderbarer als jenes, was ich gesehen habe: dieses hast du gesehen: dieses habe ich gesehen: wenn sie mich ... an ein Flüßchen(?) setzen und mit den Zähnen und Geschmack(?)[= durch Kauen und Schmecken?] lassen sie (es?) bringen, und mit den Zähnen lassen sie (es) bringen und(?) mit der Lasche (lit. Zunge) binden sie195 das Bündel: wer dieses von dir gesehen hat und jenes von dir gesehen hat: auch dir aus kleinem Leinentuch Hosen habe ich zur Jungehe(?) so wunderbar eingerichtet, und er bindet und siegelt, und wenn diese Seite offen (sein sollte?) und wenn das Bündel offen, diesem Schreiben 2 Satēr weniger in das Bündel soll(en) er (sie) bind[en ... ... daß dies ... Frēdōn ... ... ...

layers.text: An den Herrn Pērōz-Xusrō des Spihrdād, Sohn des Ritters und Helden, aus dem Dorf *Astōg(?): Verehrung! Warāz, dem Sohn des ōzōy, aus eben dem Dorf *Astōg(?) viel Gesundheit, wie Spihrdād, Sohn des Dēnīg, war aus eben dem Dorf *Astōg(?) ......... und sie haben eine Entscheidung getroffen, daß Spihrdād und den (anderen) Leuten des ... layers.text: As document of the goods: the mediators of month Ho[rdād] of the year 38: on behalf of the expenses of the family of the ōstāndār, born with inherited knowledge, to the bun of Čaharbōxt of Nēwbēhgān from Friyag who is manage in Namēwar, wheat grīw 190, grīw 50, grīw 50. From Friyag 1 sheep out of 36 lambs. To the bun of Pērōz in Anārgarān form Farrox, the manager in Namēwar, 11 sheep. On behalf of the gift for God Mihr 2 sheep. On behalf of the Amīr, who evaluated the action 1 [sheep]. From another purpose of Zādānfarrox, the overseer, piglets of Rēgān(?) 2. 1 Biryānī. 3 curd (soups?). 6 birds, small birds (?) 27. From Maškān 1 ox was brought out of 151[ ]. And wheat flour from the bun of Naxčīragān (V): Gone out from the *bath-house, month Hordād of the year 38.

               <ns0:lb n="1" xml:id="trc-p1-l1" />Dādēn guft kū 
               <ns0:lb n="2" xml:id="trc-p1-l2" />man xwāstag satēr 2 ī 
               <ns0:lb n="3" xml:id="trc-p1-l3" />abar nāmag kē ēn ayādgār 
               <ns0:lb n="4" xml:id="trc-p1-l4" />awiš wirāst ud nibišt 
               <ns0:lb n="5" xml:id="trc-p1-l5" />ēstēd az Māh-Pērōz 
               <ns0:lb n="6" xml:id="trc-p1-l6" />padīrēm ud band ī 
               <ns0:lb n="7" xml:id="trc-p1-l7" />ēn ayādgār 
               <ns0:lb n="8" xml:id="trc-p1-l8" />Dādēn (?) <rāy>
               <ns0:lb n="9" xml:id="trc-p1-l9" />pad gugāy-muhrīhā ī 
               <ns0:lb n="10" xml:id="trc-p1-l10" />Ardaxšīr ī Farrox-Husravān 
               <ns0:lb n="11" xml:id="trc-p1-l11" />āwišt </ns0:ab>
         </ns0:div>

layers.text: Dādēn a dit: Moi, l’argent de 2 satēr [= 8 drachmes] sur la lettre dans laquelle ce mémorandum a été préparé et écrit par Māh-Pērōz, je (les) reçois, et l’attache de ce mémorandum, Dādēn ...l’a scellé avec les sceaux qui en témoignent de Ardaxšīr fils de Farrox-Husravān.

layers.text: [This month Ard]wahišt (2nd month) in the year 96 day Zāmy[ād (28th day) one [... ...] by name, son of Abzūd-Xusrō, from the village of *Asp-gurd before the service of the residence at *Halīg before whom he dutifully spoke: One Dābōy by name [... ... ... from] the community of *Asp-gurd on behalf of this (case): Under the possessions of Dābōy (of) a single tillage by one ploughing ox the value of which is estimated at 15 States [and a little bit more] will give to me ... on behalf of the counsel all at once so that that money is to give to the bun of the village of *Asp-gurd 2 sections of his own land of field which produces olives of large (trees) as desired to be given to Dābōy ... now from the *produce of the land little too fragmentary ... ... ... day Zāmyād [of month Ardwahišt] in the year ... ... ... before Zurwāndādweh I will come. ... ... ] .... he sealed the promise and (for making it) legally binding the Lord put the seal over it.

layers.text: Friyag, manager in Namēwar, [from] that which (belongs) to the bun, this month Hōrdād (3rd month) of [the year] 37 concerning the ration of the mounts of Mihr-ayār-Gušnasp for the duration of ten days from the very day Ōhrmazd (1st day) until day Xwar (11th day) for each day (for) one horse, a trained Arabian, 4 kabīz (of barley), 15 bundles (of lucerne), (for) the *carriage horse 4 kabīz (of barley), 7 bundles (of lucerne), (for) the war-horse 3 kabīz (of barley), 5 bundles (of lucerne), altogether 11 grīw of barley, and 200- 70 bundles of lucerne to Xwarin given. And with the witnessesˈ seals of Dēnyadān for keeping the receipt [he con](signed it).

               <ns0:lb n="9" xml:id="trans-p1-l9" />4 kabīz (of barley), 7 bundles (of lucerne),
               <ns0:lb n="10" xml:id="trans-p1-l10" />(for) the war-horse 3 kabīz (of barley), 5
               <ns0:lb n="11" xml:id="trans-p1-l11" />bundles (of lucerne), altogether
               <ns0:lb n="12" xml:id="trans-p1-l12" />11 grīw of barley,
               <ns0:lb n="13" xml:id="trans-p1-l13" />and 200-

layers.text: Born with inherited wisdom, Ōstāndār, *beans, viz. the *harvest, on which this receipt on which this memoir (reminder) has been established and written, (viz. that) Dēnabzūd ordered to bring the container of beans which, on this day, was due to the bun, to estimate (it) this month Day (10th month) of the year 36.
